neet_che_u01_t02_1.working: Proust stated the law of definite (constant) proportions: a compound always has the same elements in the same mass ratio.

neet_che_u01_t02_2.working: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O(g), so the volume ratio is 2:1:2. With 50 mL H2, 25 mL O2 is needed and 50 mL vapour forms.

neet_che_u01_t02_4.working: A is true, since 2:1:2 is a simple whole-number ratio. R is false, because Gay-Lussac's law applies only to gases, not solids or liquids.

neet_che_u01_t02_5.working: I is correct: at the same T and P, equal volumes contain equal numbers of molecules, so the volume ratio equals the mole ratio. II is incorrect: 16 g vs 32 g of O with 12 g C illustrates the law of multiple proportions, not definite proportions.
